name: Gantry

frameLength.label: Frame length (m)
frameLength.desc: Span of the frame along its X axis, which is also the travel available to the carriage. The legs, rails and bridge all stretch with it.

frameWidth.label: Frame width (m)
frameWidth.desc: Span across the frame in Y, the second axis of travel.

frameHeight.label: Frame height (m)
frameHeight.desc: Height of the frame, which sets how far the tool can be lowered on the lift axis.

speed.label: Motion speed (m/s)
speed.desc: Top speed of a move, reached by the axis with the farthest to go. The other two are slowed in proportion so all three arrive together and the tool runs a straight line.

accel.label: Acceleration (m/s²)
accel.desc: How hard the axes ramp up to speed and brake to a stop, for the axis with the farthest to go. Lower it for a heavier or more delicate load; a short move may never reach top speed at all.

vacuumOn.label: Vacuum on (idle grip + LED)
vacuumOn.desc: Authored resting state of the vacuum: it seeds the grip and lights the status LED while the gantry sits idle. With comms on, the vacuum tag below takes over.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Connect this gantry to a PLC program. Its tags appear once this is on. Without a program the drives stay off and it holds its home pose.

mode.label: Mode
mode.desc: How the program drives the gantry. Waypoints: set the command tag to a row of the taught table and pulse Execute, like drives with stored positions. Position: write the X, Y and Z targets and pulse Execute; the gantry plans one coordinated straight-line move, like a gantry with its own controller. Follow setpoints: hold Execute and stream each axis set position every scan, for a program that runs its own motion control (an MC_MoveAbsolute per axis); the program does the coordinating.

options.label: Move to X/Y/Z (gantry plans the move)
Follow PLC setpoints (PLC plans the motion)

enableTag.label: Enable tag
enableTag.desc: Powers the drives. Drop it and the gantry stops where it is and abandons its move; raise it and it waits for the next Execute. Wire it to the cell being safe to work in. Leave it empty and the drives are always on.

commandTag.label: Command tag (0 = home, 1+ = waypoint)
commandTag.desc: Which row of the waypoint table to move to, as an index: 0 is home, 1 the second row and so on. Set it BEFORE pulsing execute. An index past the end of the table is ignored, and the arm stays put rather than guessing.

targetXTag.label: Target X tag (m)
targetXTag.desc: Where to move along the length, in metres from the frame centre. Position mode: set all three targets BEFORE pulsing execute; outside the frame, the gantry drives toward the end of the frame, stops short of it and raises Fault. Follow mode: read every scan; outside the frame, that axis parks at the end of the frame.

targetYTag.label: Target Y tag (m)
targetYTag.desc: Where to move across the width, in metres from the frame centre.

targetZTag.label: Target Z tag (m, down)
targetZTag.desc: How far to lower the tool, in metres below its raised position: 0 is fully up.

executeTag.label: Execute tag
executeTag.desc: Pulse this false-to-true to start a move. It is edge-triggered, so holding it true does NOT repeat - drop it and raise it again for each move. In follow mode, hold it true for as long as the gantry should track the targets.

doneTag.label: Done tag
doneTag.desc: Handshake back to the program: true whenever the gantry is parked and ready for the next command. Wait for it before pulsing execute again, or the edge lands mid-move and is dropped. In follow mode: true while all three axes sit on their setpoints.

faultTag.label: Fault tag
faultTag.desc: True when the last move was refused (the drives not enabled) or ended in a fault (a target past the frame: the gantry stops short of the frame end). The next Execute clears it, once the axes are still.

actualXTag.label: Actual X tag (m)
actualXTag.desc: Where the X axis is now, every scan, in the same metres as the target.

actualYTag.label: Actual Y tag (m)
actualYTag.desc: Where the Y axis is now.

actualZTag.label: Actual Z tag (m, down)
actualZTag.desc: How far the tool is lowered now.

gripperTag.label: Vacuum tag
gripperTag.desc: Grip or release the load. Read continuously rather than on an edge, so hold it true for the whole carry and drop it only once the load is where it belongs.

waypoints.label: Waypoints (row 0 = home)
waypoints.desc: Positions in frame-local metres, one row each: x along the length, y across, and z the lift measured DOWNWARD (larger is lower). Row 0 is home and the command tag picks a row. A value outside the frame parks at its limit.
